Personally, rice is my favorite grain to eat. But it requires more specific conditions and more labor to grow than other grains, so I would not pick it.

Potatoes produce the greatest number of calories per acre of farmland, and they're probably the easiest to harvest, so I suppose the pragmatist would pick them. But to me, it seems like potatoes would get boring after having nothing else for a long time, as they seem less versatile in the number of things you can do with them. Also, there's the issue of blights causing potato famines, which sucked for the Irish, and would suck for me too. Also they're harder to store than other options. So I would not pick them.

Corn produces the second greatest number of calories per acre of farmland, and it's easy enough to harvest and store. It's not particularly disease-prone, as far as I'm aware. But it seems suspicious to me that corn is nowadays mostly made into animal feed. I highly suspect it's not the healthiest thing for humans to eat on a long-term basis. So I don't pick it.

Oats have the most protein per calorie of the grains, which is worth factoring in. But I firmly believe that plant proteins are vastly inferior in terms of bioavailability to animal proteins, so that's not a huge deal to me. Other than that oats seem roughly equal to wheat.

But wheat has one thing on oats that makes me pick it, and that's versatility. No other grain makes nearly as good bread as wheat does, for reasons that escape me at the moment. Something to do with the gluten binding to the other protein or something. And there's so many other things you can do with wheat flour too! Pancakes, pasta, cakes, crackers, cream of wheat cereal. Look, maybe I'm biased towards the grain my ancestors chose, maybe an Asian would say rice is far superior and worth the extra effort and sacrifice in versatility. And maybe he would be right. But I like wheat and I'm sticking with it.

Now for the animals. I'll keep it short though, since this is getting long already.

Pigs- I know for a fact that pigs produce the greatest amount of calories per acre of farmland. Although I'm guessing most of that is fat. But pork is another one of those things that I suspect is not so great for health when consumed as a dietary staple. And pigs don't produce anything of value other than their meat. Maybe you could drink their milk if you had to, but no society has ever done it large-scale that I'm aware of, so I'm guessing it's not very good.

Cows- cows are great in that they produce a lot of protein, both in their meat and their milk. But cows are picky about the land they are pastured on, and they require lots of care. Too much effort for a young colony. Pass.

Chickens- chickens produce lots of protein in their meat and their eggs. Their feathers don't seem to be useful for much. Plus I want dairy. So, pass.

Goats- look, nothing against goats. They're cool. They're cute as babies, and they do mostly take care of themselves. But they just don't produce a lot of meat. So I'll pass on them too.

Sheep- finally, here's my choice. Sheep are a good source of meat, and of wool, which could be critical if this planet is cold. And you can drink their milk, and make cheese out of it. Feta was originally sheep cheese. They require a bit more care than goats, but still way less than cows. Sheep are good all-around, I'd say.

TL;DR I pick wheat and sheep.
